question.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{3}{y}\,i-\frac{2}{x}\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation $9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=36$ oriented counterclockwise.
question.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our curve as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1.
$$

The closed curve $C$ is the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $2$ and $3,$ respectively. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

$$
r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\frac{3}{y}\,i-\frac{2}{x}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-2-3 \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(-5)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-5t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-5(2\pi )-0 \\  & =-10\pi \end{aligned}
$$
